protocol_v2.title: Eval protocol v2: fair, production-faithful (data unblocked; building now)
items: M3.1 hub access logs from S3 (both load balancers, 5-minute parts). Measured window = the 24 h peak hour, 09-28 16:00–17:00 UTC; the 4 hours before it are warm-up. Same model era, prompts, tools and output lengths as production.

Sessions (prompt_cache_key) hashed into 24 buckets; one bucket = what one of the 24 nodes serves, whole sessions, real timestamps. Production's own per-request cached tokens and TTFT kept for comparison.

Warm-up length chosen by convergence (1 / 2 / 4 h). HiCache on, as in production. Cache-consistent replay: after each response, prime the cache with the logged answer (max_tokens=1), so later turns hit as they did in production.

Gateway drops null-valued tool-schema keywords (production accepts a tool with "maximum": null; our engine rejected 41 of 2,317 warm-up requests). Logged image bytes are redacted to /base64/: replace with a synthetic image of similar size. Every other request replays byte-for-byte.

At 1×, per-request cache hit within ~2 points of production's (96%) and TTFT distribution within 2× of production's for the same requests; report the miss breakdown (first-seen / divergence / eviction).
Load scaled by users, at real time
k× = k session buckets merged at their real timestamps, not time compression. Ladder 1× (one node's share of the peak, ≈ 5.8 req/s) to 4× in 0.5× steps.
TTFT p50 ≤ 1.0 s, TTFT p99 ≤ 15 s, per-stream decode p50 ≥ 60 tok/s, errors < 0.1% (production at its peak: 0.35 s, 10.2 s, 100 tok/s, 0.06%).

Primary: SLA capacity = highest passing k, as TPM per GPU, next to production's 24 h peak (3.38 M/GPU). Secondary: closed-loop saturation on a disjoint window (never on prompts already replayed). Appendix: static frame. Each headline run twice to show noise.
